Convert a move2 object to a list of ctmm telemetry objects

Source: R/mt_as_telemetry.R
mt_as_telemetry.Rd

This function converts a tibble of tracks (a move2 object) into the telemetry objects used by the package ctmm to fit continuous-time movement models. One telemetry object is created for each track, and the objects are returned as a list named by track id, in the same order as the tracks in the metadata (see show_meta()). The reverse conversion is provided by move2::mt_as_move2().

Usage

mt_as_telemetry(x, error_cols = "auto", ...)

Arguments

x

A move2 object, in a projected CRS with units in metres.

error_cols

The columns of the event data with information on the error of the locations, to be passed to ctmm. If "auto" (the default), the columns with a name that ctmm recognises as error information (with Movebank naming, e.g. gps_hdop, eobs_horizontal_accuracy_estimate, argos_lc, or the time to fix gps_time_to_fix, used with timeout) are passed. Otherwise, a character vector of column names, or NULL to pass no error information. ctmm ignores columns with names that it does not recognise (see ctmm::as.telemetry()); such columns can be renamed by naming the vector with the names used by ctmm, e.g. error_cols = c(HDOP = "my_hdop_column").

...

Additional arguments passed to ctmm::as.telemetry() (e.g. timeout or dt.hot).

Value

A list of ctmm telemetry objects, one per track (with at least one location), named by track id and in the order of the metadata.

Details

ctmm requires coordinates in a projected coordinate reference system (CRS) with units in metres. If x is in longitude/latitude, it should first be projected with sf::st_transform(); an appropriate CRS for the area covered by the tracks can be found with crstools::suggest_crs(). The telemetry objects use the CRS of x, and their x and y columns are the coordinates of x, so that any object estimated by ctmm (e.g. a utilisation distribution) is aligned with the original data.

Events with an empty geometry (i.e. no location) are dropped, and so are tracks without any location.

Only the track id, time and location of each event are passed to ctmm by default, plus any columns with information on location error (e.g. GPS dilution of precision or Argos location classes) that ctmm can use in an error model (see error_cols). Other columns are not passed as ctmm identifies columns by name, so that a column such as tag_local_identifier could be mistaken for the id of the track.

Examples

# the buffalo dataset from ctmm, converted to a tibble of tracks
data(buffalo, package = "ctmm")
buffalo_tt <- mt_as_move2(buffalo)
# and converted back to a list of telemetry objects
buffalo_tel <- mt_as_telemetry(buffalo_tt)
#> Minimum sampling interval of 3 minutes in Cilla
#> Minimum sampling interval of 2 minutes in Gabs
#> Minimum sampling interval of 2 minutes in Mvubu
#> Minimum sampling interval of 3 minutes in Pepper
#> Minimum sampling interval of 2 minutes in Queen
#> Minimum sampling interval of 5 minutes in Toni
names(buffalo_tel)
#> [1] "Cilla"  "Gabs"   "Mvubu"  "Pepper" "Queen"  "Toni"
